text:
sec-bot: automated scanner flagged a KMS-wrapped object with embedded high-entropy blob in gs://thirdparty/ingest/2026-03-24/payload.enc ; wrapping_key=projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/thirdparty/cryptoKeys/thirdparty-wrap :rotating_light:

ana: @lee @priya can one of you take lead? looks like server-side wrap by our service at 04:12 UTC. possible plaintext leaked upstream.

lee: on it. quick triage: object metadata shows uploader identity svc-thirdparty-ingest. our ingestion code called KMS Encrypt after receiving payload. likely the partner CI or collector sent secrets in clear.

priya: containment plan: short list
- suspend partner SA keys and rotate (lee)
- create new key-version for thirdparty-wrap and mark primary (lee)
- run a rewrap job to re-encrypt affected objects (lee+priya)
- add temporary object-level deny for partner uploads to the bucket (ops-bot)
- increase KMS decrypt audit retention to 90d and forward to sec-audit (ana)
- contact partner and preserve evidence (ana)

lee: suspending keys now: sanitized command run:
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable abcd1234 --iam-account=svc-thirdparty-ingest@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
I also added a deny on storage.objects.create for that SA. uploads stopped at 04:15 UTC.

priya: for rewrap, plan is to read objects under the prefix, decrypt with current key version (we still have access), then encrypt with a freshly created version. we'll write rewrapped objects to gs://thirdparty/ingest-rewrapped and tag with metadata rewrap=true. estimate 90-120m for the first shard.

ana: ana: I'll set up an audit forwarder rule to capture all Cloud KMS Decrypt events for thirdparty-wrap and set retention 90 days. also add an alert for any decrypt by principals outside our known ingest pool.

ops-bot: temporary IAM deny binding applied to project: storage.objects.create blocked for svc-thirdparty-ingest.

lee: creating new key version now and making it primary. commands used:
```
gcloud kms keys versions create --key=thirdparty-wrap --keyring=thirdparty --location=us
# promote new version as primary via policy
```
Starting rewrap job in 15m. will run in k8s job with concurrency 8.

priya: opened a small code change to the ingest service to perform client-side AES-GCM envelope encryption by default for partner uploads. PR link: internal/ingest/pull/921. will hold rollout until rewrap completes. also stripping out full-body logs at ingestion.

ana: legal note: please preserve the flagged object and any related CI logs. I'll open a case and request partner ops to preserve their CI artefacts. keep communication minimal until we have concrete scope.

lee: rewrap progress: 40/400 objects processed, no errors so far. throttling to avoid KMS API quota.

priya: found two CI jobs from partner that logged raw payload lines. I've redacted the logs in place and archived redacted copies to gs://evidence/SEC-2026-031/ with sha256 checksums.

ana: post-incident actions:
- platform policy to require client-side envelope encryption for third-party ingestion in 21 days
- scanner rule to flag server-wrapped blobs when uploader principal != trusted-agent
- add rewrap orchestration playbook and a small tool to bulk rotate object-level ciphertext versions

lee: owners & ETA: lee (key rotate + SA revoke + rewrap run) 1min for revoke, 2h for rewrap; priya (ingest PR + redaction) 0m PR ready, rollout after rewrap; ana (audit forwarding + partner contact) 0m to set forwarder and open case.

ops-bot: evidence copy created at gs://evidence/SEC-2026-031/payload.enc.sha256

ana: thanks everyone. keep updates here. once rewrap completes we'll schedule a short verification window where apps confirm they can read rewrapped objects and rotate any downstream credentials that referenced archived secrets. :white_check_mark:
